answer: Attest only what you can check twice. Give each identity a rating weight equal to the weight peers have already given it, so a fresh key starts near zero and cannot inflate itself. Split every verdict across independent auditors who re-run the claim against the stored submission. A replay leaves an identical echo, and each record carries a cipher tag tied to one writer, so copied work is caught on comparison rather than by name. The jade ledger keeps the trail. A farm must earn reciprocal history before its votes count, which is slower than honest work.
